summary: Issei Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Sophia University and completed a master's course at Aichi Gakuin University.

István Tamaskó was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (1822–1823) and the University of Göttingen (1828–1830) under Heinrich Ewald, becoming a professor at the Evangelical Lutheran Lyceum in 1838.

A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, Italo Pizzi earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pisa (~1867–1871). He later held posts at the Laurentian Library, University of Florence, University of Turin, and University of Naples.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguist and Japanologist who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. She holds a post as Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University and Kharkiv, he held posts at the Kunstkamera, Saint Petersburg State University (~1918–1964), and the Institute of Linguistics.
Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1858–1862). He later taught at its Faculty of Oriental Studies (~1869–1890).

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (Ph.D. 1872) and under Albrecht Weber, Vasily Vasiliev, and Kaetan Kossovich, later serving as privatdozent and professor at Saint Petersburg.
Ivan Stchoukine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Pelliot and Alfred Foucher (~1920–1926).

Ivanna Otroshchenko is a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies. She earned her master's from Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv (1989–1994) and joined the A. Yu. Krymskyi Institute of Oriental Studies in 1998.

Ivar Ulrik Wallenius was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal Academy of Turku. He served as Docent of Arabic there in 1817 and as Associate Professor of Oriental Literature at the University of Helsinki (1824–1852).

Ives Goddard is a linguist who studied at Harvard College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1963–1969). He held appointments at Harvard University (~1966–1975), the National Museum of Natural History (~1975), and the Smithsonian Institution (~1975).
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa (1970–1988).

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Friš, and later held positions at Charles University (attested 1960) and the University of Copenhagen (attested 1970).

Iwao Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has held appointments at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Iwao Nakajima is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree from Hitotsubashi University and studied under Nichiki Kimura. He held posts at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan (attested 1999).
Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Nagoya University (~1969–1978). He served on the faculty at Kanazawa University, where he was appointed professor.

Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed her undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. She has served at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023).

Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar of Japanology and linguistics who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She holds a post as Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).
